newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG AND SEIZINGER SHOPPING FOR CHRISTMAS WINS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG AND SEIZINGER SHOPPING FOR CHRISTMAS WINS.

text.p: Pernilla Wiberg and Katja Seizinger won't be expecting any gifts from each other during the final weekend of alpine World Cup races ahead of the Christmas break.
With a downhill, a slalom plus the season's first combined event up for grabs both women will be shopping for three wins and the lead in the overall standings.

Seizinger, the reigning overall champion, holds what would appear to be a healthy 112 point advantage on her Swedish rival, but could see it disappear faster than Buzz Lightyear from department store toy shelves with Wiberg favoured in two of the three events.
Friday's downhill will be the first of the season in Europe and the first at this popular Swiss resort in a decade.

Wiberg, already a proven technical skier with an Olympic giant slalom and a world championship slalom title on her resume, has demonstrated this season that she can also be a formidable force in the speed events.
The 26 year-old Swede claimed the first super giant slalom race of the season in Lake Louise and finished second to Seizinger in the downhill.
She also posted the second fastest time in the first of two downhill training runs on Thursday.
Wiberg established herself as Seizinger's main rival just as everyone thought the German was about to run away with the overall title for a second year.

The rivalry, however, is not a new one. In 1994 the two women fought it out to be runner-up behind Vreni Schneider and the Swede has made no secret she covets the crystal globe which goes to the overall champion.
The snag is that Seizinger, who in the four previous years before winning the title finished second twice and third on two other occasions, is in no hurry to give it up.
Another weekend like the one last year in Val d'Isere when she won three races in as many days could see the 24 year-old German put her stamp on a second overall title.
Even by Seizinger's own high standards, she has been in superb form.
She already has two wins this season and reached the podium five times in eight races.
